commands.text: Go down the stairs?

Descends one floor. Dungeon maps are authored so that map id == depth + 1 (G1 enforces it), so the next floor down is session.floor + 2. There is no depth cap in code: the deepest map simply carries no stairs event.
You are whisked away...
Recovery site. RECOVERY_XP_BONUS grants its carriers bonus XP for resting here (Scholar-type passives); creatures without the trait get 0 and no message.
The soothing light restores your party's HP and MP!
(She fiddles with a loose thread on her apron, waiting for you to speak.)
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: Laura? She’s… she’s amazing. She’s strong, and beautiful, and… and she smells like vanilla and iron. Is that weird? That’s weird. Forget I said that.
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: I sell things that keep you alive! It makes me happy. Watching people leave with full bags… it means they might come back. That’s nice.
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: Me? I’m just Alicia. I like baking. And… I like listening to the rain. The dungeon is scary, but the rain makes it sound like it’s sleeping.
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: I’m going to make this into a necklace. Or maybe a ring? No, a necklace. She doesn’t like rings when she works. Thank you again!
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: The Glittering Teardrop… please be careful. It’s pretty, but the dungeon is mean. Don’t get hurt for a rock, okay?
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: You… you found it! Oh, look at it! It’s perfect. It catches the light just like her eyes when she’s happy. Thank you! Thank you so much!
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: I’m going to make this into a necklace. Or maybe a ring? No, a necklace. She doesn’t like rings when she works. Thank you again!
commands.speaker: Alicia

elseCommands.text: Actually… can I ask a favor? It’s about Laura. I want to give her something special. Something that… shines like she does. There’s a crystal, a ‘Glittering Teardrop’, deep in the dungeon. Would you…?
elseCommands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: The Glittering Teardrop… please be careful. It’s pretty, but the dungeon is mean. Don’t get hurt for a rock, okay?
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: You… you found it! Oh, look at it! It’s perfect. It catches the light just like her eyes when she’s happy. Thank you! Thank you so much!
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: I’m going to make this into a necklace. Or maybe a ring? No, a necklace. She doesn’t like rings when she works. Thank you again!
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: (She wipes soot from her forehead, giving you a brief moment of attention.)
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Alicia? She's... soft. Too soft for this place. But she makes good bread. And she doesn't ask stupid questions. I tolerate her.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Fire purifies. Metal obeys. People... people lie. Steel never lies to you. It just is. That's why I like it.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: I'll need time to work on this. Check back later. And... thanks.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Find that signet. Don't come back empty-handed.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: You found it. Hmph. Not bad. The gold is pure... untouched. Give it here.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: I'll need time to work on this. Check back later. And... thanks.
commands.speaker: Laura

elseCommands.text: You're going deep? Listen. Rumor says a rare undead down there wears a golden band. Unmarked, untarnished. I want that signet — new material for my forge, good pay for you. Interested?
elseCommands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Find that signet. Don't come back empty-handed.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: You found it. Hmph. Not bad. The gold is pure... untouched. Give it here.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: I'll need time to work on this. Check back later. And... thanks.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Oh! H-hello there! It's good to see you again. Please, look around. And— uh— drink water. People forget.
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: Back again? Blade dull already? Or are you just looking for warmth?
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Crossing Writ verified. Keep your MP above the red line. Don’t be a hero in there— heroes become stains.

Descends one floor. Dungeon maps are authored so that map id == depth + 1 (G1 enforces it), so the next floor down is session.floor + 2. There is no depth cap in code: the deepest map simply carries no stairs event.
You are whisked away...
People come back talking about ‘treasure’. Then they stop sleeping. Then they stop talking. Then we stop calling them by name. Go.
A copy of your room? Keep your key. Sleep somewhere else tonight. No, I don't care where.
And if you hear yourself moving around in there before you open the door, come find me.
A hot meal below the chasm? Don't eat anything the Labyrinth cooks. It learns you through the mouth.
That blue border was used in town before the chapel roof fell. Nobody sells it now.
INES. Blue chalk. I was a child when she went below.
She returned three times. On the fourth, only her creatures came back.

elseCommands.text: Still alive. That's progress enough for today.

commands.text: Strange? Always. But the supply shipment is late. Very late. It usually comes through the old tunnel, but it's silent.

elseCommands.text: No Crossing Writ, no descent. Speak to the Registrar in the Passage Office. The rule is older than either of us.
elseCommands.speaker: Gate Guard

commands.text: The wax is still on the stones. One lantern burned until morning. Nobody admits it was theirs.
commands.speaker: Gate Guard

commands.text: The gate opens onto a town you do not quite recognize. Colored lamps hang from the roofs. Nobody is dressed for work.
commands.speaker: Gate Guard

commands.text: Back alive. Good. If you are going down again, eat something first.
commands.speaker: Gate Guard

elseCommands.text: Beyond this gate, the boundary between souls gives way. Keep hold of your name. Your creatures can fight for you, but only you can keep summoning yourself.
elseCommands.speaker: Gate Guard

commands.text: Small village. Old chapel. Bad soil. The Labyrinth pays for what the fields cannot.
commands.speaker: Gate Guard

commands.text: The chapel smells of cold wax and wet flowers. A single unclaimed lantern rests beneath the bell rope.
The card bears one name: THESTRA. The ink is fresh. The handwriting is yours.
The chapel doors stand open. Candlelight pours across the square, and names have been tied to the eaves on narrow cards.
At dusk, St. Maria closes its shops. Bakers, guards, children and scavengers gather without being called.
The first bell names the living. When Agnes speaks your name, the village answers: RETURNED.
At midnight, lanterns are carried to the Labyrinth gate. The second bell names those who remain below.
After the final name, something beneath St. Maria rings a third time.
Every flame bends toward the gate. One extinguished lantern relights by itself.
Agnes nods. "The village can wait. It has practice."
commands.speaker: Sister Agnes

elseCommands.text: The chapel is cool and nearly empty. Someone has left a bucket beneath a leak in the roof.

commands.text: Three bells. There are only two in the tower. I checked before you arrived.
commands.speaker: Yukio

commands.text: I observed. Attendance implies belief.
commands.speaker: Yukio

commands.text: You mistake possession for sentiment. A common Summoner's error.
commands.speaker: Yukio

elseCommands.text: So you're the Summoner everyone keeps glancing at. I wondered whether you would be taller.
elseCommands.speaker: Yukio

commands.text: Unfortunately. Yukio. I came from the north road this morning, which means they have spent all day confusing us.
commands.speaker: Yukio

commands.text: Their gaze moves briefly to your creatures—not dismissively, but as if counting a hand of cards.
The Tankard is open late for cleanup. Half the village is helping; the other half is pretending not to have a headache.
The bartender stops wiping the same cup. "Two bells," she says. "You heard two."
The tables are outside, the shutters are open, and the bartender is wearing a red coat you have never seen before.

elseCommands.text: The bartender remembers your drink. Nobody applauds your return this time.
The Rusty Tankard smells of cheap ale and roasted meat.

commands.text: "The Vigil." The bartender studies your face. "Nobody told you? No. I suppose we never do."
Alicia is scraping wax from a tray. One small lantern, hidden behind the counter, bears no human name.
commands.speaker: Alicia

elseCommands.condition: flag:vigil_active or flag:milestone_return_1 or flag:milestone_return_2 or flag:first_return

commands.text: Alicia is dressed in white and gold instead of her apron. She is laughing with a customer and does not notice you at first.
commands.speaker: Alicia

elseCommands.text: You came back! Sorry—everyone keeps saying that as if we doubted you. I saved you a honey roll.
elseCommands.speaker: Alicia

elseCommands.text: Oh! You're the new Summoner. I'm Alicia. Please drink water before you descend. People return looking like they forgot they have bodies.
elseCommands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: "You already did. She sent the cloth back folded into a perfect square." Alicia looks absurdly pleased by this.
commands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: "It's the warm bundle in your hands." Alicia peers over the counter. "Please don't take it into the Labyrinth."
commands.speaker: Alicia

elseCommands.text: Alicia ties bread, cheese and a bruised pear into a cloth. "Laura forgets lunch when the forge is busy. Don't say I said she forgets."
elseCommands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: "The old rule says they don't need them." She covers the hidden lantern with a cloth. "Old rules can be lonely."
commands.speaker: Alicia

elseCommands.text: "They're for the Vigil." Alicia pauses. "The village remembers people who don't come back. Officially, summons aren't included."
elseCommands.speaker: Alicia

commands.text: Laura looks at the warm cloth bundle, then at you. "She recruited the Summoner as a delivery service. Efficient."
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: She takes it with extraordinary care. "Tell her the pear was unnecessary." A pause. "Don't actually tell her that."
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Laura presses 25G into your palm as a delivery fee. It is still warm from the forge.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Laura's forge is cold. She is hammering old lantern frames flat for reuse.
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Laura's forge is cold for the first time since you arrived. She has washed the soot from her face and seems annoyed that you noticed.
commands.speaker: Laura

elseCommands.text: Back already? Sensible. Bring me anything the Labyrinth failed to digest.
elseCommands.speaker: Laura

elseCommands.text: New Summoner? Don't buy a heroic weapon. Buy something that still works while you're running home.
elseCommands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: "Open flame stays at the chapel tonight." Laura folds her arms. "St. Maria mourns beautifully. Then it sends somebody else down."
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Laura examines the sealed reliquary carefully. "Old St. Maria craftsmanship. I'll take it off your hands for 800G."
commands.speaker: Laura

commands.text: Climb toward St. Maria?
A narrow blue seam opens through the boundary.
ESC: Skip

Every few years, a Summoner
comes to St. Maria.
You did not come alone.

Saban carried you through the rain.
He was your mount—and your only summon.

St. Maria noticed him
before it noticed you.

The village made room.
Barely.

One bed. One bowl.
Five empty rooms.

Below the town, every bond
is recorded as a debt.

Beyond the gate, souls lose
their edges.

You came for impossible things.
The first was already beside you.

ST. MARIA
Late Autumn

PASSAGE HOUSE — ROOM 3

"This'll be home for both of you." The key is still turning in the lock outside when the footsteps begin to recede.
The other Summoner rooms are empty. Yours has been cleaned, but not emptied of its previous lives. Someone has dragged a feed bowl in from the stable.
Saban noses the bowl, then leans his familiar weight against you. He carried you to St. Maria; now your mount and only summon will carry you below it.

43.name: Enter First Stratum - The Bellroot Depths

commands.text: The iron gate parts without a sound. Cold air climbs the steps, carrying the echo of a bell struck far below.
